{{nihongo|'''Ajiko Shrine'''|阿治古神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Izu Province]].

It is considered a candidate shrine listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Engishiki}}. Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=shrine ranking system}}, it was ranked as a {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284|lt=former village shrine}}. The main annual festival is held from July 19 to July 21, and the Ajiko Shrine {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kashima Odori}} performed during the festival is designated as an intangible cultural property of Atami City.

=== Enshrined deities ===
* {{ill|Amaterasu|Q455602|qid=Q455602}} (Amaterasu Omikami)
* {{ill|Ame-no-Tajikarao|Q849412|qid=Q849412|lt=Tajikarao-no-Mikoto}} (Amenotajikarao)
* {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|Q317997|qid=Q317997|qid=Q317997|lt=Hondawake-no-Mikoto}} (Hondawake-no-Mikoto)
* {{ill|Takuhadachiji-hime|de|Yorozuhatahime|ja|栲幡千千姫命|ru|Ёродзухататоёакицуси-химэ-но микото|zh|栲幡千千姬命|qid=Q11110848}} (Takuhatachijihime-no-Mikoto)

(Note: On {{ill|Izu Ōshima|ar|إيزو أوشيما|az|İzuoşima|be|Ідзу-Осіма|ca|Izu Ōshima|ceb|Ō Shima (pulo sa Hapon, Tōkyō-to)|cs|Izu Óšima|de|Izu-Ōshima|es|Izu Ōshima|et|O-shima|eu|Izu Ōshima|fa|ایزواوشیما|fi|Izu Ōshima|fr|Izu ō-shima|it|Izu Ōshima|ja|伊豆大島|ko|이즈오섬|lt|Idzu Ošima|my|အိုးရှိမမြို့၊ တိုကျို|pt|Izu Ōshima|ro|Izu Ōshima|ru|Идзуосима|simple|Izu Ōshima|sk|Óšima (ostrov)|sv|Izu-Ōshima|tl|Ōshima, Tokyo|tr|Ōshima|uk|Ідзу-Осіма (острів)|vi|Izu Ōshima|zh|伊豆大島|qid=Q1070580}}, there is {{ill|Omiya Shrine|Q131925939|qid=Q131925939|lt=Omiya Shrine}}—whose former name before relocation due to volcanic eruption was Ajiko Shrine—where Ajiko-no-Mikoto, the eldest son of {{ill|Mishima Taisha|el|Μισίμα Τάισα|fr|Mishima-taisha|ja|三嶋大社|tr|Mishima Tapınağı|zh|三嶋大社|qid=Q650772|lt=Mishima Daimyojin}} and “Habun no Oho-ugo” (Hafuhime-no-Mikoto), is enshrined. Therefore, it is possible that the Ajiko Shrine in Ajiro once functioned as an evacuation branch shrine or a distant worship site, though the relationship between the two shrines is currently unclear.)

=== History ===
The founding year is unknown. It is identified as Ajiko Shrine listed among the {{ill|List of Shikinaisha in Izu Province|Q11380552|qid=Q11380552|lt=Shikinaisha}} in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}, located in {{ill|Izu Province|Q860928|qid=Q860928}}{{ill|Kamo District, Shizuoka|Q961511|qid=Q961511}}. However, another prominent candidate shrine is {{ill|Omiya Shrine|Q131925939|qid=Q131925939|lt=Omiya Shrine}} on {{ill|Izu Ōshima|ar|إيزو أوشيما|az|İzuoşima|be|Ідзу-Осіма|ca|Izu Ōshima|ceb|Ō Shima (pulo sa Hapon, Tōkyō-to)|cs|Izu Óšima|de|Izu-Ōshima|es|Izu Ōshima|et|O-shima|eu|Izu Ōshima|fa|ایزواوشیما|fi|Izu Ōshima|fr|Izu ō-shima|it|Izu Ōshima|ja|伊豆大島|ko|이즈오섬|lt|Idzu Ošima|my|အိုးရှိမမြို့၊ တိုကျို|pt|Izu Ōshima|ro|Izu Ōshima|ru|Идзуосима|simple|Izu Ōshima|sk|Óšima (ostrov)|sv|Izu-Ōshima|tl|Ōshima, Tokyo|tr|Ōshima|uk|Ідзу-Осіма (острів)|vi|Izu Ōshima|zh|伊豆大島|qid=Q1070580}}, which enshrines Ajiko-no-Mikoto. Originally, the shrine was located on Mt. Asahi to the south of the Ajiro settlement, but it was relocated to its present site closer to the village sometime before 1647 (Shoho 3).<ref name="由緒書">“Yui-shogaki,” Ajiko Shrine</ref>

The Takasugi family, who serve as the shrine priests of Ajiko Shrine, also historically served as priests of {{ill|Hatsuki Shrine|ja|初木神社|qid=Q119929623}} on nearby {{ill|Hatsushima|arz|هاتسوشيما|az|Hatsuşima|ceb|Hatsu-shima|de|Hatsushima|fr|Hatsu-shima|ja|初島|ko|하쓰시마섬|zh|初島|qid=Q689643}} to the east. The family possesses the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Goshintai}} ({{ill|kakebotoke|ja|懸仏|qid=Q108461401}}) of Hatsuki Shrine, believed to date back to the Kamakura period.<ref>[https://www.hatsushima.jp/find/history.html History of Hatsushima] – Fuji Kyuko Marine Resort</ref> (Today, the rituals of Hatsuki Shrine are conducted by {{ill|Izusan Shrine|fa|معبد ایزوسان|fr|Izusan-jinja|ja|伊豆山神社|zh|伊豆山神社|qid=Q611460}}, which is connected through the myth of Hatsukihime.<ref>[https://www.hatsushima.jp/find/legend.html Legends of Hatsushima] – Fuji Kyuko Marine Resort</ref><ref>[https://atamii.jp/today/113728/ Hatsushima / Hatsuki Shrine annual festival, Kashima Odori dedicated, praying for island safety and a good catch] – Atami Net Newspaper, 2019/7/19</ref>)

In 1591 (Tensho 18), {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|Q187550|qid=Q187550}} carried out the {{ill|Siege of Odawara (1590)|Q2622890|qid=Q2622890}}.<ref name="由緒書"/> Hideyoshi ordered Ajiro Village to provide military ships to attack Atsugi Castle, and 30 vessels were dispatched from Ajiro.<ref name="由緒書"/> After Atsugi Castle fell successfully, Hideyoshi rewarded Ajiko Shrine, granting permission to use banners dyed with the “Nagare-hyotan” (flowing gourd) pattern and to wear swords.<ref name="由緒書"/> Even today, during festivals, the sacred boat “Ryomiyamaru” (Ryomiyamaru) and its attendants use banners bearing the flowing gourd emblem.<ref name="由緒書"/> Furthermore, it is said that during the reign of {{ill|Tokugawa Iemitsu|Q314481|qid=Q314481}}, when the shogunate’s ceremonial ship {{ill|Atake Maru|Q11450528|qid=Q11450528}} was towed to {{ill|Edo|Q215646|qid=Q215646}}, the Tokugawa shogunate granted permission to use “white streamers.”<ref name="由緒書"/>

On September 1, 1923 (Taisho 12), the {{ill|aftermath of 1923 Great Kantō earthquake|Q3742341|qid=Q3742341}} occurred, causing the shrine buildings of Ajiko Shrine to collapse.<ref name="由緒書"/> In July 1926 (Taisho 15), the current shrine buildings were completed at a cost of 35,000 yen.<ref name="由緒書"/>

In 2020 (Reiwa 2), the annual festival was canceled due to the impact of the {{ill|COVID-19 pandemic|Q81068910|qid=Q81068910|lt=global outbreak of COVID-19}}. In 2021 (Reiwa 3), it was canceled for a second consecutive year for the same reason.

=== Festivals ===
The annual festival is held every year from July 19 to July 21 (or the nearest weekend), with the 19th as the eve festival, the 20th as the main festival, and the 21st as the concluding festival.<ref name="由緒書"/> On the final day, the “Ajiro Bay Festival” is held at {{ill|Port of Ajiro|Q11607165|qid=Q11607165|lt=Ajiro Fishing Port}}.<ref name="taga-kanko"/><ref>[https://atamii.jp/today/御神船「両宮丸」２０日に網代を渡御-２１日にべ/ Sacred boat “Ryomiyamaru” parades through Ajiro on the 20th, Bay Festa on the 21st – Atami Ajiko Shrine annual festival] – Atami Net Newspaper, 2019/7/18</ref>

During the annual festival, a divine procession takes place in which the sacred boat “Ryomiyamaru,” carrying a {{ill|Mikoshi|Q979940|qid=Q979940}}, parades through the town of Ajiro.<ref name="ataminet">[https://atamii.jp/today/113771/ Sacred boat “Ryomiyamaru” parades valiantly through Ajiro, resounding with shouts of “Yaa-Yaa”] Atami Net Newspaper, July 20, 2019</ref> Banners dyed with the “Nagare-hyotan” flowing gourd pattern, permitted by {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|Q187550|qid=Q187550}}, and “white streamers” permitted by the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tokugawa shogunate}} are used.<ref name="由緒書"/> The procession is also simply called “the Ajiro Festival.”

The Ajiko Shrine Kashima Odori is also performed during the annual festival, but writing down the song lyrics is forbidden, and they are passed down orally.<ref name="由緒書"/> Along the eastern coast of the {{ill|Izu Peninsula|Q822822|qid=Q822822}}, there are many regions that perform {{ill|kashima odo|Q11677163|qid=Q11677163}}.<ref name="由緒書"/>
